transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Head of ML, Zenith IO), Diego Martinez (Platform Eng), Nora Patel (CTO)
---
00:00 Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll hand it off to ethan in a sec to show the console but quick intros — i'm maya, i'm the account owner, and ethan is our solutions engineer.
00:12 Laura Chen: hi, thanks — excited to see the per-route stuff, we've been trying to get a clearer per-endpoint cost breakdown.
00:18 Ethan Ross: great, yeah i'll share my screen. real quick recap of your use case: embeddings + vector search at multi-tenant scale, peak QPS around 400, average latency target 150 ms p50 and 350 ms p95, is that still correct?
00:34 Laura Chen: yes that's right. and for compliance: we need SOC2, SSO, and some data residency requirements in eu-west.
00:42 Ethan Ross: noted. ok screen share starting... bear with me, i have two monitors.
00:58 Ethan Ross: so this is the Console home, top-level usage analytics. you'll see overall tokens, embedding units, and a per-route breakdown here. i've preloaded a demo tenant that mimics your traffic so the numbers look realistic.
01:20 Diego Martinez: can you zoom into the per-route dashboard? specifically we want to see cost per route and how batching impacts it.
01:28 Ethan Ross: sure. click routes -> per-route. loading... okay there we go. each row corresponds to a route — in our demo tile we have /embed-search, /chat-assist, /rerank.
01:45 Ethan Ross: notice the columns: requests, average latency, p95, token consumption, and cost estimate. cost is broken down by model variant and infra — so hosted vs dedicated pricing estimate.
01:56 Laura Chen: how accurate is that cost estimate? our finance team needs near accurate unit economics before a pilot.
02:05 Ethan Ross: good question. the console uses actual runtime telemetry combined with per-model token costs to estimate spend. it's accurate to within the margin of the model pricing — there's some approximation for batching benefits which we model using your traffic profile. if you give us your traffic CSV we can run the calibrated model to get closer numbers.
02:28 Nora Patel: is that the same model you used for the benchmarks you sent last week? i saw a sheet but couldn't tell if it matched our sequence length distribution.
02:36 Ethan Ross: it's a different default sheet; i'll share the exact benchmark CSV we used for the demo. it has sequence length distributions and the kernel selection assumptions. i'll drop the sheet after the call.
02:48 Maya Patel: quick pause on product names — sometimes they show as redwood-optimize or redwood-ops in the sheet, the transcript might say rewood, etc, but the important part is that the console surfaces per-route suggestions for batching and quantization.
03:05 Diego Martinez: when you say 'suggestions' can you show an example? like what's a recommended batch size for /embed-search?
03:12 Ethan Ross: yes; over on the right pane there's an optimize recommendation card. for /embed-search, given 768 token embeddings and a typical payload, it suggests batch size 16 for lower cost with minimal latency impact; and if you need sub-100 ms, we can lower batch to 4 but cost goes up 25%.
03:30 Laura Chen: that tradeoff is exactly what we need to present to product. do you show projected monthly spend for both configurations?
03:36 Ethan Ross: yep — toggle the 'cost scenarios' dropdown and choose 'aggressive batching' vs 'low latency' and it recalculates projected monthly spend based on your traffic.
03:47 Ethan Ross: i'll switch to the timeline view so you can see token usage and spikes, that helps with capacity planning.
04:00 Ethan Ross: here on the timeline you can also annotate events — deployments, holidays, marketing blasts — which helps explain bursts and makes cost forecasts more accurate.
04:12 Diego Martinez: nice. question about reserved capacity — if we reserve Dedicated GPUs, does the console show expected savings?
04:18 Ethan Ross: yes, Dedicated shows an alternate column. we model committed vs on-demand and show estimated savings; usually 20-40% depending on commit level and burst patterns.
04:30 Laura Chen: and what about fallbacks? if Dedicated is saturated do you show how requests are routed to hosted?
04:36 Ethan Ross: there's a routing policy simulator — open the routing tab — you can flip policies to prefer latency, cost, or proximity. the console will simulate fallback scenarios and display expected latency and cost impacts.
04:50 Nora Patel: from a security/regulatory perspective, how do you demonstrate data residency and audit logs? we're not comfortable sending embeddings out of region.
04:59 Maya Patel: good point. we have private deployments and VPC options; audit logs and KMS integration for keys. i'll attach our security pack but ethan can show the logs.
05:12 Ethan Ross: right, under observability -> audit logs, you get token-level traces, who called what, and exportable logs. there's also an SSO mapping view for RBAC; we can scope access per route.
05:26 Laura Chen: do you capture prompt-level logs by default? that's sensitive for us.
05:31 Ethan Ross: by default we capture telemetry and token counts, not full prompts for hosted. for Dedicated/Private we support configurable retention and can redact or disable prompt capture, and integrate with your KMS for envelope encryption.
05:47 Diego Martinez: can we run our own quals — like run a benchmark from our infra against your hosted endpoints?
05:53 Ethan Ross: absolutely. we typically do a pilot where we run your benchmark suite against the selected model variants and configs, and we compare latency and cost; we'll provide the benchmark harness and can run it with either hosted endpoints or a dedicated pool.
06:08 Laura Chen: timeline wise — we want pilots running by late january. is that feasible?
06:14 Maya Patel: yes the typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. we'll need a short intake, sample traffic, and a decision on whether to go hosted or dedicate capacity.
06:25 Nora Patel: one other question — how do you measure quality regressions if we change model versions? we need to tie regressions to prompts.
06:33 Ethan Ross: redwood has built-in eval sets and quality monitoring you can tie to your prompt tests. the console will alert on regression drifts and you can associate rollouts with canary traffic to measure A/B metrics.
06:47 Diego Martinez: back to cost — can i get a CSV export with per-route by day granularity? finance will want that.
06:53 Ethan Ross: yes, export button on the per-route view. i'll include that CSV in the follow-up along with a short walkthrough video.
07:02 Laura Chen: any limitations with quantized models for embeddings? we care about recall.
07:08 Ethan Ross: good callout — for some quantization profiles we preserve embedding fidelity; the console suggests quantization profiles per model and includes a small eval (cosine similarity) so you can see expected recall delta. for strict recall you can pin a full-precision variant.
07:25 Maya Patel: quick interruption — i see a chat in the background — sorry if that's loud.
07:30 Nora Patel: no worries.
07:35 Ethan Ross: going to demo the cost scenario compare side-by-side. watch the projected monthly spend for /embed-search as i toggle batching.
07:46 Ethan Ross: toggled to 'low latency' — projected spend $7.2k/mo. 'balanced' — $4.8k/mo. 'aggressive batching' — $3.6k/mo. numbers are illustrative for demo tenant.
08:10 Laura Chen: that delta is helpful. can you annotate which parts of cost are model tokens vs infra?
08:16 Ethan Ross: yes the stacked bar breaks down into model cost, GPU infra, and networking. hover over to see absolute amounts.
08:25 Diego Martinez: on infra — what GPU families do you show in Dedicated? our infra team prefers A100-80GB for some workloads.
08:33 Ethan Ross: Dedicated supports several instance types; the console will show per-model recommended kernel and preferred instance family. for embedding-heavy workloads we often recommend A100 or H100 depending on throughput needs.
08:46 Nora Patel: if we go private/on-prem, do you still get the console?
08:50 Maya Patel: yes, we provide a private control plane option; the console can be run in your VPC with the same dashboards, just data stays in-region.
08:59 Laura Chen: great. any SLA numbers you can share quickly?
09:03 Maya Patel: for Dedicated we have latency and uptime targets in the SLA — i'll include the SLA summary in the follow-up. hosted API has best-effort but we can attach SLOs for enterprise.
09:15 Diego Martinez: a practical question — what telemetry do you need from us to model batching accurately?
09:21 Ethan Ross: ideally a CSV with timestamped request logs including route, payload size, sequence lengths, and arrival time. 7-14 days of representative traffic is perfect.
09:31 Laura Chen: we'll prepare that.
09:34 Maya Patel: quick recap before we close — action items: i'll send pricing SKUs and security docs, ethan will share benchmark CSV and per-route video, laura will upload traffic profile, and we'll lock a pilot kickoff week.
09:47 Nora Patel: that works for us. thanks for the clear demo.
09:52 Maya Patel: thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with links.
---
End of transcript.
Notes on transcription quality: some product names and acronyms slightly off (redwood-optimize vs redwood optimize), filler words and overlap present.
Shared artifacts referenced during call: demo console link (redwood.app/console/demo-tenant), benchmark spreadsheet (will be attached), security pack (redwood-security-pack.pdf).
